ja:shirotae.note: White cloth of mulberry bark; a set epithet for white things, robes and snow.

ja:momiji.note: Autumn leaves, from momitsu, 'to turn red or yellow'.

ja:iro.note: Color, and also love and sensual beauty. Komachi's poem means both at once.

ja:kurenai.note: Crimson from safflower. The name means 'the dye of Kure (China)'; kara-kurenai is 'Chinese crimson'.

ja:kurokami.note: Black hair, long and glossy, a mark of beauty in Heian poems.

ja:sumizome.note: 'Ink-dyed': the grey-black of a monk's robe.

zh:huang.note: Yellow, the color of earth and of the emperor.

zh:cui.note: Kingfisher green, from the bird's bright blue-green feathers.

zh:bai.note: White; also bright, clear and plain.

zh:qing.note: The color of nature: blue, green, even black (青絲, black hair). One word where English needs three.

zh:hong.note: Red, from pink to scarlet: flowers, blushing faces, rouge.

zh:bi.note: Jade green or jade blue: deep water, a clear sky, green jade.

zh:lan.note: The indigo plant. 'Green as lan' may mean its green leaves or the blue dye made from them; readers still argue.

zh:caose.note: 'Grass color': a green you can see from far off but not up close.

zh:yin.note: Silver. The Silver River, 銀河, is the Milky Way.

zh:sese.note: A blue-green gemstone; here the shaded half of the river.

el:melas.note: Black or dark: the earth, ships, blood, wine.

el:chloros.note: The pale green-yellow of new shoots, also of honey, sand and a face drained by fear. It means fresh and pale as much as green.

el:porphyreos.note: A dark, heaving gleam: the surging sea, blood, death. Later the purple of murex dye. The word may describe motion as much as hue.

el:rhodo.note: 'Rose-fingered', Dawn's stock epithet: the pink streaks of first light.

el:erythros.note: Red. Ereúthetai, 'it reddens', is the same root.

el:leukos.note: White, but first of all bright and gleaming.

el:kyaneos.note: Dark, blue-black. From kyanos, a dark blue glaze or stone; Homer gives it to brows, clouds and ships.

el:polios.note: Grey, grizzled: the grey sea, grey hair.

el:kroko.note: 'Saffron-robed', Dawn's other epithet. Saffron gave a deep yellow-orange dye.

el:ion.note: The violet flower. 'Violet-haired' or 'violet-crowned' may mean dark, glossy hair or a garland; nobody is sure.

el:oinops.note: 'Wine-faced': the wine-dark sea. Whether it names a darkness, a sheen or a hue is still argued; it doesn't show the Greeks couldn't see blue.

la:viridis.note: Green, and also fresh and young.

la:pallidus.note: Pale, wan; in flowers, a pale yellow-green.

la:niger.note: Glossy black. Ater is the dull, gloomy black.

la:candidus.note: Dazzling, shining white. Albus is the plain, matte white.

la:luteus.note: Yellow, the dye of the weld plant.

la:ater.note: Dull, gloomy black, the color of death and mourning.

la:purpureus.note: Purple, the murex dye, but also simply 'glowing': Horace has purple swans.

fa:lale.note: The tulip or wild red tulip, Persian poetry's emblem of red, often of blood.

fa:lal.note: Ruby or red spinel: the beloved's lips, and red wine.

fa:zard.note: Yellow; also the pale face of a lover or the sick.

fa:sabz.note: Green; also fresh and flourishing, and the first down on a young cheek.

fa:arghavan.note: The Judas tree, whose red-purple blossom names a color.

fa:banafshe.note: The violet flower; the color word banafsh comes from it.

fa:firuze.note: Turquoise. 'The turquoise vault' is the sky.

it:perso.note: Dante's dark purple-black. In the Convivio he calls it a mix of purple and black in which black wins.

ja:akaaka.note: 'Red, red': the blaze of a low sun.

ja:ao.note: Blue and green together; a green traffic light is still 'ao'.
